researched.description: AI clinical intelligence platform generating notes, care plans, and outcomes for CCBHCs and nonprofit behavioral health teams
researched.notes: Real licensed AI platform, but the site names nonprofit behavioral health teams, CCBHCs, group practices and individual therapists as its market - no government or public agency buyer is named.

researched.description: Janet data platform that replicates and reports on Credible EHR data for behavioral health agencies
researched.notes: Janet is a real product but it is an add-on to a commercial EHR sold to behavioral health agencies generally, alongside the firm's consulting work; government is not a named primary market.

researched.description: Anonymous feedback kiosks and dashboards for shelters, behavioral health providers, and community health organizations to hear from the people they serve
researched.notes: Genuine hardware-plus-software product, but the who-we-serve page lists eleven nonprofit and community-provider segments and names no government agency, city, county or public department as a market.

researched.description: Performance measure data collection and dashboard system for federal grantees, including SAMHSA SUPRT and SPARS reporting
researched.notes: Subscription software, but the site targets "organizations receiving federal grants" rather than naming government buyers, and it is sold beside parent firm The Policy & Research Group's evaluation and technical-assistance consulting.

researched.description: Live online tutoring, writing feedback, and test prep delivered through public libraries, school districts, and colleges
researched.notes: Instruction vendor - the deliverable is live academic support from human expert tutors delivered through a web portal, not a licensed software product.

researched.description: Freegal music streaming, VOX audio-enabled books, ebooks, and language learning products for public libraries and schools
researched.notes: Content vendor - Freegal, Freading and Pure Flix are licensed music, ebook and film catalogs, and VOX Books are physical audio-enabled books; libraries are buying content and goods, not software.

researched.description: Classical music and opera video streaming licensed to public libraries, schools, and universities for patron access
researched.notes: Content vendor - the product is a licensed catalog of concert, opera and ballet films sold as a library database subscription, delivered through a web portal.

researched.description: WorldCat shared cataloging, discovery, resource sharing, and library management systems for public, academic, school, and research libraries
researched.notes: Self-described nonprofit, member-driven library cooperative of ~30,000 member institutions whose core offering is the WorldCat shared bibliographic database plus membership, research and community programs - two supplier triggers (nonprofit/association and licensed database) outweigh its hosted services.

researched.description: Library management, digital archive, institutional repository, and research data management systems for academic and research libraries
researched.notes: Confirmed product company - licenses four named software systems (TIND ILS, DA, IR, RDM) with public university and public-institution libraries (UC Berkeley, Indiana, Univ. of Chicago) as the named primary market.

researched.description: Student information system and education ERP for colleges and universities covering admissions, academics, finance, and reporting
researched.notes: Confirmed - licensed cloud SIS/ERP whose only named market is higher education institutions (400+ institutions), placed in Gartner's SIS SaaS Magic Quadrant.

researched.description: Series25 academic and event scheduling, space management, and admissions application software for colleges and universities
researched.notes: Confirmed - named licensed products (Series25, 25Live, Schedule25, LYNX, X25) sold exclusively to colleges and universities.

researched.description: AI platform for university enrollment operations covering transcript evaluation, applicant communication, and CRM and SIS integration
researched.notes: Confirmed - SaaS platform billed as the AI operating system for higher education, 120+ university clients, no market named outside higher ed.

researched.description: Course evaluation, survey, and AI feedback analysis software - Blue, MLY, and Metrics That Matter - for universities and corporate learning teams
researched.notes: Real product company, but the site sells feedback and survey analytics to three co-equal markets - higher education, corporate HR/employee engagement, and general organizations - so education is one segment among everyone else.

researched.description: Enterprise AI platform that unifies SIS, LMS, and CRM data and governs AI agents for colleges and universities
researched.notes: Confirmed as a platform, not the consultancy it grew out of - the site sells one intelligence layer over SIS/LMS/CRM addressed to university presidents, CIOs and CFOs, with higher education as its only named market.

researched.description: Claimed AI conversational teaching platform; current offering could not be confirmed
researched.notes: Site returns placeholder-level content on both the homepage and /about - no product, market or customer information available to verify either the product test or a government/public-education market.
